newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Sterling seeks break of $1.66 support.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Sterling seeks break of $1.66 support.

text.p: Sterling seeks to slice through the $1.66 level which has limited its downside for more than a week, paving the way for a move to $1.6450, analysts said.

The pound remains bolstered against the mark, however, and is expected to top the five-year high of 2.9100 it reached overnight. Analysts expect sterling to overcome minor hurdles at 2.9140/85 marks and surge to the 2.9475 high set in May 1992.

"The repeated failure to break back above the $1.6725/70 area indicates we are consolidating with a heightened risk of a deeper pullback," said Francoise Skelley, the head of global trading technical analysis at Credit Suisse First Boston.
"There has been entrenched support at $1.66/6580 but the dollar is going to go up so there is a bigger risk of a break down in cable."
The pound was at $1.6654/64 at 0748 GMT from $1.6640/45 late Monday in Europe. Sterling/mark was at 2.9080/85 from 2.9026/36 late yesterday.

Cable has tested $1.6600 every day for the past five trading days and rebounded on each occasion. However, each time, it has lacked the momentum to extend its gains and break above $1.6725, the five-month high it set on June 23. Stop-loss orders to sell pounds are therefore likely to have been left below $1.6580.

Still, support should cut in at $1.6450, which marked the upper band of congestion between the end of May and late June, according to Gerry Celaya, the senior technical strategist at American Express Bank.
Expectations of a pull back in cable have not dampened optimism about sterling's outlook against the mark, though.

Sterling/mark is expected to encounter interim resistance at in the 2.9140/85 area, according to Skelley at CSFB. She predicts that this will prove a temporary obstacle and sees little to hold sterling back from powering on to 2.9475 marks. -Swaha Pattanaik, London newsroom +44 171 542 6284
